transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brought me in is... I keep hearing this man’s voice. It comes right out of the garage vents at work, and sometimes from under the hood when I'm working on a vehicle, clear as somebody standing right next to me. He keeps telling me not to trust my husband, and not to touch certain cars. 

Which is a real problem because I'm a mechanic, you know? I have to touch the cars. I was working on this '08 Civic the other day, just doing a basic alternator swap, and the customer had left all these fast food wrappers piled up in the passenger seat. I don't understand how people can let their cars get that dirty. It just smelled like old fries and stale coffee. My husband is kind of messy like that too, honestly. He leaves his socks everywhere in the living room, and I'm always the one picking them up after I get home from a ten-hour shift. He bought this new mechanical keyboard for his computer that clicks so loud it drives me absolutely crazy when I'm trying to watch TV... but anyway, yeah, the voice just keeps coming out of the vents telling me I can't trust him.
Do you see anything unusual that other people don't see?

See things? No, not really. I mean, my vision is fine, though I do need to get my safety glasses replaced at the shop. They got this massive scratch right down the middle of the left lens when I was under a Chevy truck last week. The rust just falls right in your face if you aren't careful. 

My manager, Dave, is supposed to order the new safety gear, but he's always dragging his feet. He just sits in the back office scrolling on his phone all day. I saw him looking at fiberglass fishing boats online yesterday. Who buys a boat right now? The economy is terrible and gas prices are insane. I spend like sixty dollars just filling up my own truck, and the gas station by my house is always out of receipt paper at the pump, so I have to go inside every single time. I hate going inside because the guy at the counter always tries to talk to me about the lottery, and I don't even play the lottery. It's just a tax on people who are bad at math, my dad used to say that all the time... um... what were we talking about? Did you ask me about my truck?
Do you feel like your thoughts are well-organized, or do you find it hard to stay on one topic when talking?

My thoughts? No, I think they're perfectly organized. I don't have any trouble staying on topic at all. You kind of have to be organized in my line of work, you know? If you aren't keeping track of everything, you're gonna lose your 10-millimeter socket. Everyone always loses the 10-mil. It's like a running joke at the shop, but it's not funny when you're paying Snap-on prices to replace it. 

The Snap-on guy, Greg, he came by on Tuesday trying to sell me this massive neon green tool chest. I don't know why anyone would want a neon green tool chest, it just shows the grease so much faster. Plus, his truck always smells so strongly of that Black Ice air freshener. It's so overpowering, it gives me a massive headache. I bought one of those little cardboard tree air fresheners for my husband's car once, just a vanilla one, but he threw it straight in the trash because he said the smell bothered him. He's so picky about smells. He won't even eat at this one diner we used to go to on weekends because he says the booths smell like old bleach, which is a real shame because they have the best hash browns. They get them really crispy on the edges, just how I like them, and they give you those little glass bottles of ketchup instead of the plastic squeeze ones. I always struggle getting the ketchup out of the glass ones, though, you have to hit the 57 right on the neck of the bottle... I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Did you want to know about my husband?
Have you ever heard voices like this before, outside of the situation at work?

No, it's just the man at work. Just coming out of the vents at the shop, or from under the hood when I'm working on a car. It's so clear, just like you and me talking right now, telling me not to trust my husband and not to touch certain cars. Which is really frustrating because, like I said, I have to touch the cars. 

I was working on a Subaru Outback yesterday, one of the newer ones, and the oil filter is right on top of the engine now. It's so much easier to get to than the older models where you had to reach up past the exhaust manifold and burn your arm. I have this scar on my forearm from a hot exhaust pipe from like three years ago. It's shaped exactly like a crescent moon. My niece thought it was a tattoo when she saw it at Thanksgiving. She's seven, and she's obsessed with the moon and space and all that. She wants to be an astronaut, which I think is great, but my sister keeps telling her she needs to focus on her spelling tests first. My sister is always so strict about school stuff. She used to make me do my homework before I could even take my shoes off when we got home from the bus stop. We lived at the end of this really long dirt road, and the bus would kick up so much dust... wait, did you ask about my sister?
How do you feel when you hear the voice telling you not to trust your husband or touch certain cars?

How do I feel? I mean, it's terrifying. It's exactly why I came in here in the first place. I just keep hearing this man's voice coming from the garage vents, and sometimes right out from under the hood when I'm working. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, telling me not to trust my husband or touch certain cars. And it makes me feel so on edge, especially about the cars, because if I don't work on them, I don't get paid. 

And we really need the money right now because our water heater just completely died on Sunday. We woke up to this massive puddle in the basement, right soaking into the boxes of winter clothes I hadn't unpacked yet. All my good wool sweaters, just drenched. Wool is so heavy when it's wet, and it smells like wet dog, even if you don't own a dog. We used to have a golden retriever when I was a kid, Buster, and he would always jump in the creek behind our house and then come inside and shake water all over the floral wallpaper in the kitchen. My mom hated that wallpaper anyway, she said the yellow flowers looked like mold, but my dad refused to take it down because he spent a whole weekend putting it up in the eighties. He was so stubborn about DIY projects. He tried to fix the plumbing once and we didn't have a working toilet for three days... um... wait, what did you ask me? Did you want to know about my dad?
When the voice tells you not to trust your husband or touch certain cars, does it tell you what will happen if you don't listen?

No, it doesn't really say what'll happen. It just... it's just telling me not to do it. Like I was saying, that's what brought me in, because I keep hearing this man's voice coming from the garage vents, and sometimes right from under the hood. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, telling me not to trust my husband or touch certain cars. 

But no, it never gives a reason. It's just a warning. Which makes it even harder to ignore, you know? Like, what if something bad does happen? I'm already so careful around the lifts at the shop. My boss, Dan, he's always harping on safety protocols because this one guy, years ago, before I even started working there, dropped a whole transmission on his foot. Shattered every bone. They had to put pins in it and everything. I can't even imagine the medical bills for that. Dan said the guy tried to sue the shop, but he wasn't wearing his steel-toed boots that day, so it didn't go anywhere. I always wear my steel-toes. They're heavy, though, my feet are killing me by the end of the day. I tried buying those gel insoles, but they just made my boots too tight and my toes went numb. Have you ever had your toes go numb? It's the weirdest feeling, like walking on bubble wrap... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my boots?
Do you believe the voice is trying to tell you something true about your husband?

I mean... yeah. I know it sounds far-fetched, but I'm still convinced he is. My husband and my boss, Dan, they've been using the EV chargers and the security cameras at the shop to track what I'm doing. They keep showing me the footage and saying there's nothing there, but I know they are. The EV chargers have all these smart features now, they connect right to the Wi-Fi. We installed three of them last month because we're getting more electric cars in. 

Electric cars are so quiet, it's actually kind of creepy. You don't even hear them pull into the bay. One snuck up on me last week and I almost dropped my wrench. I have this really nice set of Snap-on wrenches, they cost a fortune but they're guaranteed for life. My grandpa gave me my first set of tools when I was twelve. He had this massive red toolbox in his garage, and it smelled like grease and old coffee. He used to drink his coffee black, no sugar, no nothing. Said it put hair on your chest. I tried it once and spit it all over his driveway. It was so bitter. I have to have at least two sugars in mine, and that vanilla creamer. The French vanilla one, not the hazelnut. Hazelnut tastes like dirt to me. My husband bought the hazelnut one by accident last week and I had to go back to the store... um... wait. What did you ask me? Did you want to know about my husband?
Do you think the voice is real or is it just your mind playing a trick on you?

I mean, it has to be real, right? That's what brought me in, because I keep hearing this man's voice coming from the garage vents, and sometimes right from under the hood. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, telling me not to trust my husband or touch certain cars. It doesn't sound like a trick, it sounds like a real person. 

And you know, vents carry sound so well. In our old apartment, before we bought the house, we could hear everything our upstairs neighbors were doing through the bathroom vent. They used to play this thumping bass music at two in the morning. It drove me absolutely crazy because I had to be at the shop by six. I tried leaving a polite note on their door, but they just ignored it. People are so inconsiderate sometimes. Like people who don't use their turn signals. It's not that hard, it's just a little flick of the wrist! I see it all the time when I'm test-driving customer cars. I always test-drive them after a brake job, you have to make sure the rotors aren't warped. Warped rotors make this awful shuddering feeling in the steering wheel. It's really dangerous on the highway, especially in the rain. I hate driving in the rain, the glare from the headlights on the wet pavement gives me a migraine. I usually have to take two ibuprofen and lie down in a dark room... wait, what did you ask me? Did you want to know about my migraines?
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that weren't there when you were alone or in a different environment, not just at work?

Well, mostly it's at the shop, like I said. That's really what brought me in, because I keep hearing that man's voice coming from the garage vents, and sometimes right from under the hood of the cars. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, telling me not to trust my husband or touch certain cars. But I guess... I guess I've heard it a couple times at home, too. Like when I'm in the garage there. 

We have a two-car garage at the house, but we can only fit one car in it because my husband has all his woodworking stuff on the other side. He makes these birdhouses out of cedar. They're actually really pretty, he sells them at the farmer's market on weekends. The farmer's market is great, they have this one stand that sells homemade sourdough bread. I try to get there early before they sell out, because there's nothing better than warm sourdough with real butter. Not margarine, it has to be real butter. My mom used to buy margarine when I was a kid and it always tasted like plastic to me. She was always trying to save money, clipping coupons from the Sunday paper. The ink would get all over her fingers and she'd leave black smudges on the kitchen counter. I hated cleaning those up. I use this citrus degreaser at the shop that works miracles on grease, I wonder if it would work on newspaper ink... um... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about the garage at home?
Have you ever heard any other voices or sounds that weren't there before you started hearing the voice at work?

No, not before this. I mean, the voices and this whole thing with them tracking me, it's all been happening for about ten months now. So nothing before that, really. Ten months... yeah, because that was right around the time we had that massive heatwave. The AC at the shop completely died on us. Let me tell you, working in a service bay with no air conditioning is absolutely brutal. You get sweat dripping right into your eyes while you're under a chassis, and your safety glasses get all fogged up. I actually had to order these special anti-fog ones online. Amazon is super convenient, but the delivery drivers always leave the boxes right in front of my garage door at home. They just drop them right where you could back over them! My husband actually ran over a package last year, it was a box of those cedar blocks he uses for his birdhouses. Completely crushed them into splinters. He was so mad, he spent like an hour on the phone with customer service. I hate calling customer service, you just get stuck on hold listening to that awful elevator music that sounds like it's playing underwater... um... wait. What were we talking about? Did you ask me about the shop's AC?
Do you often find yourself jumping from one topic to another while talking, like you have today?

Well, I guess I do jump around a bit, but it's just because I have so much to say and it all connects in my head. Like, once I start explaining my plans or trying to tell someone what's been happening with the voices and the tracking, the words just pour out of me. It's so fast, my husband and the guys at the shop are always telling me to slow down and take a breath. But stopping feels almost impossible, you know? It's like a faucet you can't turn off. 

Speaking of faucets, the one in the shop's break room has been dripping for weeks. It's this steady 'drip, drip, drip' that drives me up the wall when I'm trying to eat my lunch. I told the manager he needs to replace the O-ring, it's literally a fifty-cent part and takes five minutes to fix. But he's so cheap, he won't even buy decent coffee for the machine. We have to drink this generic brand that tastes like burnt dirt. I usually stop at the gas station on the way to work to get a large iced coffee instead. I have to get it with almond milk though, because regular dairy makes my stomach upset. I tried oat milk once, but it has a weird aftertaste, almost like cardboard. Have you ever noticed that? Cardboard boxes always smell so strange when they get wet, kind of like wet dog. My neighbor has a golden retriever that always gets loose and rolls in the mud, then shakes it all over my driveway... wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Did you want to know about my husband?
Do you feel like you're having trouble sticking to one topic when we talk?

Well, yeah, I guess I do have trouble sticking to one thing, but like I was just saying, it's because I have so much to get out. When I start trying to explain my plans, or all the stuff that's been happening—you know, with the voices and how they're tracking me—the words just pour out of me. It happens so fast. My husband and the guys at the shop are constantly telling me, "Slow down, take a breath," but stopping feels almost impossible. It's like I physically can't. 

It's sort of like when you strip a bolt on an engine block and you just keep turning the wrench, hoping it'll catch, but it just spins and spins. I had to drill out a stripped bolt on a Honda Civic last Tuesday. The customer was so mad because it took an extra hour, but what was I supposed to do? You can't just leave a broken bolt in the cylinder head. The guy was wearing this really loud Hawaiian shirt, too. Bright orange with these massive purple hibiscus flowers all over it. I don't know where people even buy shirts like that. Probably at one of those tourist trap shops down in Florida. My aunt went to Florida last winter and brought me back this snow globe with a flamingo inside. Who puts a flamingo in a snow globe? It doesn't even snow there! Although, with global warming, who knows anymore. The weather's been so crazy lately. We had hail the size of golf balls last spring. It completely dented the hood of my truck... um... wait. What were you asking me? Did you want to know about the truck?
Do you think the voice is something that other people could hear if they were in the same situation as you?

Well, I mean, it's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, so yeah, I think if someone was standing right where I was, they'd have to hear him. It's this man’s voice, and it comes right out of the garage vents at the shop, or sometimes from right under the hood of a car I'm working on. He tells me not to trust my husband, or he warns me not to touch certain cars. It's so loud and real. 

But speaking of the vents, they really need to get the ductwork cleaned at the shop. The amount of dust and grease that blows out of those things is ridiculous. I swear I've been sneezing non-stop. I actually bought this heavy-duty air purifier for my bedroom to make up for it, one of those expensive HEPA filter ones. It has this little blue ring of light on top that glows when the air is clean, but my cat absolutely hates the light. She always tries to swat at it when she walks by the nightstand. She's a calico, and you know what they say about calicos having a lot of attitude. My sister had a cat like that who used to steal socks right out of the laundry basket and hide them under the sofa. We found like thirty mismatched socks when we helped her move out of her apartment. Moving is the absolute worst, honestly. The boxes are so heavy, and you always end up hurting your lower back. I had to use a heating pad for a solid week last time we moved... um... wait, sorry. I lost my train of thought again. What did you just ask me? Did you want to know about the air purifier?
Do you think the voice you're hearing could be coming from your own thoughts or mind, rather than an external source?

No way, it's definitely not just my own thoughts. I mean, that's literally what brought me in here to see you. I keep hearing this man’s voice, and it's coming from the garage vents, or sometimes right from under the hood of a car I'm working on. It is as clear as somebody standing right next to me. He tells me not to trust my husband, or he warns me not to touch certain cars. 

Speaking of certain cars, I was looking under the hood of this '08 Subaru Forester the other day, and the head gaskets on those things are just notorious. I mean, whoever designed that boxer engine really didn't think about the mechanics who actually have to fix them. You basically have to pull the whole engine out just to get to the gaskets properly. My dad used to have a Subaru back in the 90s. It was this ugly forest green color with rust all around the wheel wells. We drove it all the way to Yellowstone one summer. Yellowstone is gorgeous, but the sulfur smell near the geysers is just awful. It smells exactly like rotten eggs. I actually accidentally left a carton of eggs in the trunk of my car after a grocery run last July, and oh my god, the smell when they baked in the sun for three days... I had to use three bottles of upholstery cleaner just to get the stink out of the trunk carpet. Carpet cleaner always smells like fake lemons, you know? Kind of like that cheap hard candy they give out at the bank... um, wait. What were we talking about? Did you ask me about the Subaru?
Do you think your way of talking and jumping between topics makes it difficult for others to understand what you're trying to say?

Yeah, I suppose it does make it hard for them. Like I was saying earlier, once I start explaining my plans or all the things that have been happening, the words just pour out of me so fast. My husband and my coworkers are always telling me to slow down, but stopping just feels almost impossible. 

It really is like when you have completely shot brake pads. You press the pedal and there is no friction at all, just metal on metal grinding, and you just cannot stop the car. I had a guy bring in a Chevy Tahoe last week with rotors that were ground down to absolute dust. He claimed he did not hear the squealing. How do you not hear that? I bet he just turns his radio up way too loud to ignore it. I used to blast the radio when I was a teenager, mostly classic rock stuff. My dad had this massive collection of cassette tapes in his garage. I read online that cassettes are actually making a comeback now. People are buying them up at thrift stores. I love thrift stores, honestly. You can find the best vintage denim jackets there. I found this one jacket with a huge embroidered eagle on the back, but it smelled so strongly of mothballs I had to leave it. Mothballs always remind me of my grandmother's attic... um, wait. Sorry. What were we talking about? Did you ask me about the brakes?
Do you often feel like your thoughts are racing and you can't control what you're saying?

Yeah, exactly. That's exactly how it feels. My thoughts are just zooming, like a hundred miles an hour, and I can't catch them, let alone control what comes out of my mouth. It's like I have to say everything that pops into my head the second it gets there. 

It's honestly exhausting, kind of like when you're trying to bleed a clutch line by yourself and you have to keep pumping the pedal and running back and forth to check the fluid level. Brake fluid is nasty stuff, too. If you get it on your skin, it just eats right through it. And it ruins paint. You have to be so careful not to drip it on the fenders. I always use those magnetic fender covers when I work. I got this really nice set from the Snap-on truck last month. The Snap-on guy, Gary, he always brings donuts on Tuesdays. Glazed donuts are okay, but I really prefer the ones with the chocolate frosting and sprinkles. My niece had a birthday party last weekend and they had this massive cake covered in sprinkles. It was supposed to look like a unicorn, but the horn was made out of this weird fondant that tasted like straight plastic. I don't get why people use fondant. Buttercream is so much better. I tried making Swiss meringue buttercream once, but you have to whip the egg whites forever, and my hand mixer just started smoking. It literally smelled like an electrical fire in my kitchen... wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What did you ask me? Did you want to know about the cake?
Do you think the voice you're hearing is talking about you or your life specifically, or is it just giving you general warnings?

Well, it's definitely about me and my life. Like I said, it's that man's voice, and it's always telling *me* specifically what to do. It comes right out of the vents in the garage, or sometimes from under the hood when I'm working, and it's so clear. Like, he'll tell me I can't trust my husband, or he'll warn me not to touch certain cars. 

It's weird how sound travels in a garage, though. The acoustics are so bouncy because of all the concrete and metal. We have these huge bay doors that roll up, and when they're open, the sound of the air compressor just echoes down the whole street. My neighbor hates it. He's this older guy who sits on his porch all day, just watching people. He has this massive golden retriever that barks at literally everything. Dogs are so funny like that. My cousin had a golden retriever that would only eat its food if you pretended to take a bite first. They are so food motivated. I tried to train my cat to do tricks with treats once, but she just looked at me like I was an idiot. Cats really do have this superiority complex, don't they? I think it's because they were worshipped in ancient Egypt. I watched this whole documentary on ancient Egypt last week. They used to pull the brains out through the nose when they mummified people. Can you imagine being the person whose job that was? Just going to work every day with a little hook... wait. Sorry. What was the question? Did you ask about the cats?
Do you find yourself jumping from one topic to another and having racing thoughts even when you're not at work or hearing the voice?

Yeah, it happens everywhere, honestly. Not just at the shop or when the voice is talking. Even when I'm just sitting at home trying to watch TV with my husband, my brain is just going a million miles a minute, and I'll start talking about one thing and end up somewhere completely different. 

Like the other night, we were watching this cooking show, and they were making this crazy elaborate pasta dish. It reminded me of this Italian place we went to for our anniversary last year. The food was good, but the waiter was so incredibly rude. He just threw the plates down on the table. It's like, I get it, working in the service industry is tough. I worked at a diner when I was taking a few classes at the community college, and the Sunday morning church crowd was the absolute worst. They would run you ragged for extra ranch dressing and then leave a fake twenty-dollar bill that was actually a Bible tract as a tip. I mean, who does that? It's so deceptive. It reminds me of those fake car parts you can buy online. People think they're getting a deal on an OEM sensor, but it's some cheap knockoff that fails in a week. Then they bring it to me to fix, and they get mad when I tell them they bought garbage. You really get what you pay for, you know? Like with boots. I finally invested in a good pair of steel-toe Red Wings, and my back hasn't hurt nearly as much. They take forever to break in, though. I wore extra thick wool socks for a month... um, wait. Did I answer your question? What were we talking about? The TV show?
Do you think your thoughts are disorganized or hard to follow for others?

Yeah, I guess so. My husband tells me that all the time. He says he can't keep up with me when I get going, like I'm talking in circles or just jumping around too much. It frustrates him, I think. 

He gets frustrated pretty easily, though. Like when we're trying to put together Ikea furniture. We got this new TV stand last month, and the instructions are just pictures, no words. Who thought that was a good idea? It's like trying to read ancient hieroglyphics. I was telling you about ancient Egypt earlier, right? Anyway, he put one of the panels on backwards, and we had to take the whole thing apart. He stripped two of the screws trying to force it. I told him to just let me do it, because I'm used to dealing with stripped bolts at the shop. We have this extractor set that works miracles. You just drill a little pilot hole and then the bit bites into the metal and backs it right out. It's so satisfying. Almost as satisfying as peeling the plastic film off a new phone screen. I got the new iPhone a few weeks ago because my old one fell out of my pocket while I was leaning over a radiator and it shattered on the concrete. The guy at the Apple store was so nice, though. He had this really cool tattoo of a compass on his forearm. I always wanted a tattoo, maybe like a wrench or a spark plug, but I'm terrified of needles. I can't even look when I get my blood drawn. The last time I went to the clinic, the nurse had to poke me three times because she said my veins were rolling. It left this huge purple bruise that lasted for... wait. I'm sorry, I lost track again. Did you ask about my husband?
Do you think your thoughts are more disorganized when you're hearing the voice than when you're not?

I don't really know if they're more disorganized then, because the voice doesn't really stop even when my brain slows down. Like, even during a quieter few weeks I had recently where I was sleeping a lot more and I wasn’t making any huge plans, I still heard the garage voice. And I still completely believed that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

My boss is always watching everyone anyway, to be honest. He paces around the shop floor with this clipboard, just clicking his pen. Click, click, click. It's one of those Pilot G2 gel pens. I actually really love those pens because they write so smoothly, but they smear terribly if you're left-handed. My older brother is left-handed, and when we were in school, the whole side of his hand was always shiny gray from pencil lead. We used to draw these massive, detailed maps of imaginary cities on the back of leftover wrapping paper. My mom would always buy that really cheap foil wrapping paper that tears if you even look at it wrong. I tried wrapping a torque wrench for my husband in that stuff for his birthday one year, and the metal just poked right through the ends. It looked like a shiny, crumpled burrito by the time I gave up and just shoved it in a gift bag. Gift bags are such a scam, though. They charge like six dollars for a piece of thin cardboard with string handles. I could make a better one out of shop rags and zip ties, honestly. Zip ties fix literally everything. I used one to hold up my muffler on my old Civic for like two years before I finally welded it. Welding is so relaxing once you get the puddle going just right... um, wait. Sorry. What did you ask me? Were we talking about my boss?

doctor.intent: determine if the patient experiences any other hallucinations besides hearing voices
doctor.question: Do you see anything unusual that other people don't see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations (seeing things that others don't). My symptom profile includes auditory hallucinations (hearing a voice) under S020, but it does not specify visual hallucinations.

patient.answer:
See things? No, not really. I mean, my vision is fine, though I do need to get my safety glasses replaced at the shop. They got this massive scratch right down the middle of the left lens when I was under a Chevy truck last week. The rust just falls right in your face if you aren't careful. 

My manager, Dave, is supposed to order the new safety gear, but he's always dragging his feet. He just sits in the back office scrolling on his phone all day. I saw him looking at fiberglass fishing boats online yesterday. Who buys a boat right now? The economy is terrible and gas prices are insane. Who thought that was a good idea? It's like trying to read ancient hieroglyphics. I was telling you about ancient Egypt earlier, right? Anyway, he put one of the panels on backwards, and we had to take the whole thing apart. He stripped two of the screws trying to force it. I told him to just let me do it, because I'm used to dealing with stripped bolts at the shop. We have this extractor set that works miracles. You just drill a little pilot hole and then the bit bites into the metal and backs it right out. It's so satisfying. Almost as satisfying as peeling the plastic film off a new phone screen. I got the new iPhone a few weeks ago because my old one fell out of my pocket while I was leaning over a radiator and it shattered on the concrete. The guy at the Apple store was so nice, though. He had this really cool tattoo of a compass on his forearm. I always wanted a tattoo, maybe like a wrench or a spark plug, but I'm terrified of needles. I can't even look when I get my blood drawn. The last time I went to the clinic, the nurse had to poke me three times because she said my veins were rolling. It left this huge purple bruise that lasted for... wait. I'm sorry, I lost track again. Did you ask about my husband?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thought disorder is consistent with schizophrenia
doctor.question: Do you think your thoughts are more disorganized when you're hearing the voice than when you're not?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a quieter few weeks when I was sleeping more and wasn’t making huge plans, I still heard the garage voice and believed my husband and boss were tracking me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the relationship between the patient's disorganized thoughts (a manic symptom) and hearing the voice (a psychotic symptom) to determine if the psychosis occurs independently of the mood episode.

patient.answer:
I don't really know if they're more disorganized then, because the voice doesn't really stop even when my brain slows down. Like, even during a quieter few weeks I had recently where I was sleeping a lot more and I wasn’t making any huge plans, I still heard the garage voice. And I still completely believed that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

My boss is always watching everyone anyway, to be honest. He paces around the shop floor with this clipboard, just clicking his pen. Click, click, click. It's one of those Pilot G2 gel pens. I actually really love those pens because they write so smoothly, but they smear terribly if you're left-handed. My older brother is left-handed, and when we were in school, the whole side of his hand was always shiny gray from pencil lead. We used to draw these massive, detailed maps of imaginary cities on the back of leftover wrapping paper. My mom would always buy that really cheap foil wrapping paper that tears if you even look at it wrong. I tried wrapping a torque wrench for my husband in that stuff for his birthday one year, and the metal just poked right through the ends. It looked like a shiny, crumpled burrito by the time I gave up and just shoved it in a gift bag. Gift bags are such a scam, though. They charge like six dollars for a piece of thin cardboard with string handles. I could make a better one out of shop rags and zip ties, honestly. Zip ties fix literally everything. I used one to hold up my muffler on my old Civic for like two years before I finally welded it. Welding is so relaxing once you get the puddle going just right... um, wait. Sorry. What did you ask me? Were we talking about my boss?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits prominent psychotic symptoms, including hearing voices that provide a running commentary on their life or tell them to do or not do specific things, which are characteristic of schizophrenia spectrum disorders. The presence of disorganized thinking and speech, as evidenced by the patient's frequent tangents and difficulty staying on topic, further supports this diagnosis.
